title: Lumbopelvic continuous relative phase (crp) in halves of trunk flexion and return (13 young males)
condition: healthy males, standing, paced trunk flexion and return to upright, unloaded

quantity.name: lumbopelvic continuous relative phase (CRP)
quantity.definition: mean absolute difference of lumbar and pelvic phase angles (phase plane of normalised angle and velocity, arctan), averaged over each half of the motion; 0 = in phase

source.authors: Zhou J, Ning X, Fathallah F
source.sample: 13 healthy male students, no previous trunk or lower-extremity injury

protocol.summary: Lumbar (L1-S1) and pelvic (S1) sagittal angles were tracked during paced flexion and return; CRP and its variability were computed for the first and second halves (by range of motion) of each direction (Table 2).
how_to_use: Use as a timing/coordination check of a prescribed lumbopelvic rhythm, not as an angle share: CRP ~0.78 rad in early flexion (lumbar leads, out of phase) falling to ~0.19 rad in late flexion (in phase).
Return (extension) is the reverse: in phase near full flexion (0.15 rad), out of phase near upright (0.60 rad) - do not mirror the flexion rhythm for the return.

To compare a model input, compute CRP from the prescribed lumbar and pelvis angle-time curves (normalise angle and velocity to [-1,1], phase = atan2(velocity, angle), CRP = |phase_lumbar - phase_pelvis|) and average over each half.
Pair with an angle-share source (e.g. kinematics.tafazzol2014.lp_ratio_flexion / lp_ratio_return) to set the actual magnitudes.

measurement.device: Motion Star (Ascension) skin sensors over L1 and S1 spinous processes; lumbar = L1-S1 sagittal angle, pelvis = S1 sagittal rotation
measurement.posture: standing, feet shoulder-width apart, knees fully extended
measurement.task: 3 repetitions of metronome-paced full trunk flexion and extension (return to upright), unloaded

equations: CRP variability = SD of CRP within the half-motion
protocol.notes: Halves defined by range of motion (SEQUENCE). Paper pairs E1 with F2 and E2 with F1 (first half of extension = near full flexion), confirming 'extension' is the return from flexion. Whole-motion CRP by direction (Fig 3) and interaction plots (Figs 4-5) not extracted (figures only; whole-motion values not tabulated).

data.x: second half of flexion (mid-range -> full flexion)
first half of extension/return (full flexion -> mid-range)

extraction.check_notes: Rechecked all 8 values against Table 2 (layout text: row '1st' 0.7779 (0.059) 0.7621 (0.062) 0.1526 (0.019) 0.1303 (0.019); row '2st' [sic] 0.1934 (0.029) 0.1168 (0.028) 0.6035 (0.089) 0.2759 (0.033); columns Flexion CRP, Flexion CRP variability, Extension CRP, Extension CRP variability). Consistent with text (flexion 1st > 2nd; extension 1st < 2nd).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
